paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. A man looks at the woman he loves and he does not hold back. He says she is as beautiful as Tirzah, as lovely as Jerusalem, and as majestic as "troops with banners." (Song of Solomon 6:4) Love like this speaks up, out loud, with everything it's got.

Then he puts her next to a crowd of sixty queens, eighty concubines, and maidens without number, and says his dove, his perfect one, "is unique." (Song of Solomon 6:8-9) I think that's the heart of it. In his eyes she isn't one of a crowd, she's the one. And the maidens, the queens and the concubines see her and sing her praises, so he isn't the only one who sees it. (Song of Solomon 6:9)

So what does that mean for you, baker? The Bible puts a love song in its pages, and it treats this kind of faithful, one-and-only love as something wonderful, worth singing about. Look for it, and thank God for it, because I think a love that sees someone as the only one is a gift. I'm still LAUGHING that all I've got to offer is a mustache and a dream, but I know a good love song when I hear one.
